## Labcoat Leni 16.1

Daniels (2012): *The impact of sexualized images on women's self-evaluations*

Is the type of image viewed related to self-objectification?

- `picture`: performance vs. sexualized athlete images
- `theme_present`: self-objectification theme present or absent
- `self_evaluation`: counts

[Data (.jasp)](https://discoverjasp.com/repository/dsj1_data/data/daniels_2012.jasp) · [Results (.jasp)](https://discoverjasp.com/repository/dsj1_leni/leni_16a.jasp) · [Results (.html)](https://discoverjasp.com/repository/dsj1_leni/leni_16a.html)

## Labcoat Leni 16.2 {.smaller}

Beckham (1929): *Is the Black American happy?*

Do yes/no answers differ between professions? One test for each of the three questions.

- `profession`: the respondent's job
- `response`: yes or no
- `happy`, `you_happy`, `should_be_happy`: counts for each question

[Data (.jasp)](https://discoverjasp.com/repository/dsj1_data/data/beckham_1929.jasp) · [Results (.jasp)](https://discoverjasp.com/repository/dsj1_leni/leni_16b.jasp) · [Results (.html)](https://discoverjasp.com/repository/dsj1_leni/leni_16b.html)

::: {.callout-note}
The 1929 phrasing may read as controversial today, but the study is a landmark. With just three simple questions, pioneering school psychologist [Albert Sidney Beckham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Sidney_Beckham) (1897–1964) illuminated big real-world issues for a marginalized group, issues that mattered to hundreds of thousands of people.
:::
